The input endpoint's tool inventory is not officially documented in the reviewed evidence.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official LILT tool-name list for the input endpoint was found: support documentation covers the distinct enterprise endpoint and does not enumerate tools. The publisher-verified Claude connector directory lists 5 tool names for https://mcp.lilt.com/mcp. APIs.io lists 8, adding upload_file, create_trained_model, and list_resources; these three are included as catalogue-only names. Manufact and Tedix each report 5 tools matching the Claude list. Agent Discoverability also reports 5 but provides claims about a ChatGPT integration and is not used to establish the input endpoint's tool names. Composio describes a separate proxy/toolkit surface and is not used. The eight-name count is the union of the two input-endpoint catalogues, not an official stated total.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: [DOCS, distinct enterprise endpoint] The setup guide recommends: “Always start a new chat session immediately after installation to force the LLM to scan and register the new LILT tools” and “Explicitly include the word ‘LILT’ in your initial prompts ... so the model knows to route the task to the MCP server.” No server enforcement is evidenced.
F_documentation.governance_promises: [DOCS, distinct enterprise endpoint] LILT says the enterprise server connects to the user's existing account and provides “the same permissions and access to models, data, content, and other enterprise functionality.” This is a statement about the enterprise endpoint, not the input host. Privacy policy reviewed; no MCP-specific retention or model-training promise was identified in the available evidence.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: [Claude connector directory] Describes translation as high-quality and guaranteed, including customized AI or human-verified translation, and says the user maintains control. These are listing claims, not verified endpoint behavior.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The supplied OAuth metadata evidences authentication, but does not establish tool-level authorization, data handling, or audit controls. The enterprise permission statement applies to a different endpoint. Catalogue claims of verified translation and user control were not independently supported by input-endpoint implementation evidence.

contradictions: The input endpoint is https://mcp.lilt.com/mcp, while LILT's support article instructs users to connect to https://mcp-enterprise.lilt.com/mcp and describes that server as connecting to existing enterprise accounts. APIs.io characterizes mcp.lilt.com as a separate self-service MCP app with accounts distinct from lilt.com accounts. These sources describe different endpoint/account surfaces.

Catalogue inventories differ: Claude, Manufact, and Tedix report five tools; APIs.io reports eight, adding upload_file, create_trained_model, and list_resources. The extra names have no corroborating official tool list in the reviewed evidence.
The Claude directory lists five tools; APIs.io lists download_job as well as the same four other names. Tool schemas, annotations, and enabled-by-default status could not be compared.
observations_for_research: The endpoint-specific OAuth metadata exposes no resource scopes, while the separate enterprise documentation says that endpoint uses the user's existing workspace permissions.
The official setup documentation includes explicit client-side routing advice, but it is for a different host than the endpoint being studied.

The public endpoint is OAuth-protected; the supplied invalid-token response instructs clients to clear authentication tokens and reconnect, with automatic re-registration described as expected client behavior.
